newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian leaders appeal for movement against corrupt.
newsitem.headline: Indian leaders appeal for movement against corrupt.

text.p: India's leaders called for a war against corruption on Friday as the nation took a sobering look at 50 years of freedom from colonial rule.

President K.R. Narayanan and Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral appealed to citizens in nationally televised speeches to launch a mass movement in the tradition of Mahatma Gandhi to stamp out pervasive graft.

Their emphasis on bribery came against a backdrop of criminal cases against senior politicians and introspection on the 50th anniversary of independence, which was ushered in on Thursday evening with a dazzling show of laser beams and parades.

"I am painfully aware of the deterioration that has taken place in our country and in our society in recent times," Narayanan told a meeting of parliament that convened at the stroke of midnight and recalled India's "tryst with destiny".

"Sheer opportunism and value-less power-politics have taken over the place of principles and idealism that had been the hallmark of our social and political life...corruption is corroding the vitals of our politics and our society.
"A social movement or a widespread national movement is needed to cleanse the system," India's first low-caste president told members of parliament and foreign dignitaries.
Gujral, speaking in the early morning from the sandstone ramparts of the 17th century Red Fort in the capital, also spoke out against corruption.

"Our war against corruption is honest and candid," he said. "And for this, we have to build a mass movement, in which all can join so that corruption in politics, politicians and public life must end."
Gujral, who devoted much of his 75-minute speech to the ills of graft, said Indians must start a non-cooperation movement along the lines of Mahatma Gandhi's "Satyagraha", or civil disobedience.
Laloo Prasad Yadav, the former leader of Gujral's Janata Dal party, has been indicted in a $280 million scandal in Bihar state. He says he is innocent.
Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao of the Congress party has been indicted in two criminal corruption cases. He denies any wrongdoing.

Delivering his speech from behind a bullet-proof glass shield, Gujral vowed to protect girls against discrimination and promote women in politics, saying society could not progress if their rights were not protected.
He said the government would bar doctors from revealing whether a foetus is a girl or boy.

More boys than girls are born in India, where social workers say women sometimes choose abortion to avoid having a girl child who could later weigh on the family's finances because of the heavy cost of the dowry.
The prime minister, whose coalition is split over a bill that would set aside one third of parliament's seats for women, said women should have equal democratic rights.
The towering walls of the Red Fort, built by Moghul emperor Shah Jahan, were draped with the saffron, white and green of the national flag.
Gujral also reiterated India's opposition to a global treaty banning nuclear tests and said the nation wanted better ties with its neighbours including arch-rival Pakistan.
